chapter_theme: A single song at Kandankudi (கந்தன்குடி): the poet asks Murugan to come one day on the peacock like a light filling the worlds and give his feet, so that the bonds of his trembling body and the births of a deceitful heart end; the praise shows the child playing as Siva worships and Murugan coming to save a devotee who calls him guru.

801.reading: The poet asks that one day Murugan come on the peacock, blazing like a light that fills the heavens, the cosmos, the earth and every direction, and give his red-gold feet that bring joy, so that the ties of his trembling, defective body and his sorrow end; he asks whether the births of this lonely rogue, whose heart houses deceit and always gathers faults, will not cease. The praise shows the little bells of the child's necklace sounding as he plays daily while Siva, the Sambhu, worships, and Murugan coming that day with love so that the devotee who praises him as 'Kandan, Guha, my guru' might see and be saved, at Kandankudi of pools sweet with spilled fruit.
801.nuance: The song chimes on nasal clusters (எந்தன், பங்கம், தொந்தங்களை, வஞ்சம்), and the shrine's name is echoed in the devotee's own formula கந்தன் குகன் என்றன் குரு. நெஞ்சன் துகள் என்றும் கொளும் வண்டன் தமியன்: the self-abuse is of a heart that keeps choosing fault. The devotee saved by Murugan's coming is not named.

links.note: 801 asks Murugan to come one day on the peacock and give his feet, and praises him as the one who came that day with love (அன்று அன்பொடு வருவோனே) so that a devotee who called him 'Kandan, Guha, my guru' might be saved. 810 is that coming told in the first person: the Lord taught, fed him Tamil, led him through light and nada, and came lovingly on the radiant peacock (அன்பொடு கதிர்தோகைப் பரி மேற்கொளும் செயல் மறவேனே). What 801 asks for and attributes to an unnamed devotee, 810 remembers as done to the poet.
